name: CapCut Axis Stretch Word Emphasis
use_when: One word needs extra visual attention without adding a separate sticker, arrow, or zoom.
A short hook, title, or emphasis word can stretch vertically or horizontally while staying readable.
The edit needs a trendy but simple word emphasis that can be controlled with keyframes.
avoid_when: The word is long or already hard to read.
Stretching would distort a brand font or make the typography feel cheap.
The line needs subtle, serious, or accessibility-first text.

timeline_pattern.pattern: text_layer -> disable_uniform_scale -> height_or_width_start_keyframe -> move_playhead -> height_or_width_end_keyframe -> increase_axis_value -> hold_or_return
timeline_pattern.axis_rule: Use height for vertical enlarge and width for horizontal stretch; do not stretch both unless the word still reads cleanly.
timeline_pattern.emphasis_rule: Apply to the impact word, not filler words.
timeline_pattern.restore_rule: Return to normal shape or cut away if the distorted word would overstay.

motion.rule: Stretch must be brief enough to read as emphasis, not a broken font.

keyframe_values.uniform_scale: Disable Uniform Scale before animating only width or only height.
keyframe_values.duration: Use a short social emphasis window, then hold briefly only if the word needs to register.
keyframe_values.intensity: Increase the axis only until attention rises; reject values that make letters unrecognizable.

sound.rule: A tiny pop can support the stretch only if it lands on the axis-change frame and stays below speech.

captions.rule: Do not use stretch on continuous subtitles; reserve it for designed emphasis words.

color.rule: Keep color simple because the distortion is already the emphasis.

implementation.ffmpeg: Render the word as an overlay and animate scaleX or scaleY independently; if using drawtext directly, pre-render text to an image for non-uniform scaling.
implementation.remotion: Animate CSS transform scaleX or scaleY on a Text component with transformOrigin set to the desired anchor.
implementation.blender: Animate text object scale on one axis only and apply Bezier or linear interpolation according to the desired snap.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Select the text layer, deselect Uniform Scale, add a Height or Width keyframe, move forward, add another keyframe, then increase the chosen axis value and preview at phone size.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics or a nested text layer with non-uniform Scale Width/Height keyframes or Transform effect scale controls.

common_mistakes: Stretching a long phrase instead of one impact word.
Distorting the word until it becomes slower to read.
Applying width and height changes by accident after disabling uniform scale.
Using the effect repeatedly until every word feels equally important.
qc: Is the stretched word the meaning-changing word?
Can the word still be read at the most stretched frame?
Does the effect avoid faces, proof, UI, products, and captions?
Does any SFX land on the stretch and stay below speech?
Is the text restored, held, or cut intentionally after the emphasis?
